question_text:
Lena started keeping her phone in another room while doing homework. At first she worried she would miss messages, but after a week she noticed she finished assignments faster and checked her phone less often even during breaks.

What was the main benefit Lena noticed?

options.A: She completed her homework more efficiently
options.B: She spent more time checking messages during breaks
options.C: She began doing all assignments at school
options.D: She stopped using her phone completely

explanation: The text says she finished assignments faster.

question_text:
A neighbourhood bakery began selling yesterday's bread at a discount during the final hour before closing. The owner says less food is now thrown away, and many students come specifically at that time.

Why did the bakery introduce the discount?

options.A: To attract only tourists at closing time
options.B: To reduce food waste while still selling the bread
options.C: To make fresh bread more expensive
options.D: To shorten the bakery's opening hours

explanation: The change is linked directly to throwing away less food.

question_text:
When Amir joined the school basketball team, he expected the hardest part to be fitness. Instead, he found remembering the team's plays more difficult. He began drawing them in a notebook and reviewing them before practice.

What problem did Amir have?

options.A: He disliked drawing in his notebook
options.B: He was not fit enough to join practices
options.C: He struggled to remember the team's planned moves
options.D: He could not understand the coach's instructions at all

explanation: He found the plays difficult to remember.

question_text:
The town installed digital signs at three busy bus stops. They show expected arrival times based on live vehicle locations rather than only the printed timetable. Passengers say waiting feels less uncertain.

What do the new signs provide?

options.A: How crowded each bus will be
options.B: The price of each bus journey
options.C: Only the times printed on old timetables
options.D: Updated information about when buses are likely to arrive

explanation: The signs use live locations to estimate arrival times.

question_text:
Nora used to buy bottled water every day at college. After receiving a reusable bottle, she began filling it at the campus fountains. She says the change was easy because the fountains are located near most classrooms.

Why was Nora able to change her habit easily?

options.A: Water refill points were convenient for her
options.B: She stopped drinking water outside college
options.C: A friend filled the bottle for her every day
options.D: Bottled water became unavailable in shops

explanation: The fountains were near most classrooms.

question_text:
A teacher asked students to submit the first version of an essay a week before the final deadline. The class then exchanged drafts and gave one another comments. Many students made major changes before submitting the final version.

What was the purpose of submitting an early draft?

options.A: To give the teacher less marking to do
options.B: To give students time to improve their work using feedback
options.C: To prevent students from changing their essays
options.D: To make the final deadline earlier

explanation: The early draft allowed peer feedback and later revision.

question_text:
Kai had always assumed museums were quiet places where visitors simply looked at objects. During a science museum visit, however, he tested machines, built a paper bridge and joined a short experiment. He left surprised by how active the visit had been.

What surprised Kai?

options.A: Visitors were not allowed near the exhibits
options.B: The museum was much quieter than expected
options.C: The museum involved visitors in practical activities
options.D: The museum focused only on modern art

explanation: He expected passive viewing but took part in hands-on activities.

question_text:
A small company introduced one meeting-free afternoon each week. Staff can still contact one another for urgent issues, but routine meetings must be scheduled at other times. Employees say longer tasks are now easier to finish.

Why do employees value the meeting-free afternoon?

options.A: It guarantees that no urgent issue can interrupt them
options.B: It lets them leave work earlier every week
options.C: It removes the need to communicate with colleagues
options.D: It gives them uninterrupted time for focused work

explanation: They can complete longer tasks more easily without routine meetings.

question_text:
Marta began learning new vocabulary by writing each word in a sentence about her own life. She found that unusual or funny personal examples were especially easy to remember later.

What helped Marta remember vocabulary?

options.A: Connecting new words with memorable personal examples
options.B: Writing every word several times without context
options.C: Learning only words that looked unusual
options.D: Avoiding examples connected with her own life

explanation: She used sentences about her own life and remembered unusual examples.

question_text:
The school cafeteria tested a pre-order system for lunch. Students choose meals in an app before 10 a.m. Kitchen staff can then prepare more accurate quantities, and queues at lunchtime are shorter.

What is one effect of the pre-order system?

options.A: Students must now pay before entering the cafeteria
options.B: The cafeteria can better predict how much food to prepare
options.C: Lunch has become available only through the app
options.D: The cafeteria prepares the same amount of every meal

explanation: Pre-orders give kitchen staff more accurate quantity information.

question_text:
Daniel wanted to improve his running pace, so he initially tried to run fast every day. After feeling constantly tired, he changed his plan: most runs are now easy, with only one faster session each week.

Why did Daniel change his training?

options.A: He decided that pace never matters
options.B: He wanted to train for a different sport
options.C: His original approach left him too tired
options.D: His weekly schedule had too few running days

explanation: The text says daily fast running made him constantly tired.

question_text:
A local theatre now offers a short discussion after selected performances. Audience members can ask actors and directors about choices made during rehearsals. Attendance at the discussion is optional and included in the ticket price.

What can audience members do after selected performances?

options.A: Watch a recording of the rehearsal
options.B: Buy a cheaper ticket for the next show
options.C: Join actors during the performance
options.D: Ask the theatre team about how the production was created

explanation: The discussion allows questions about rehearsal and production choices.

question_text:
Sofia used a translation app whenever she did not know an English word. Her teacher suggested first trying to describe the idea using words she already knew. Sofia says this has made conversations smoother because she pauses less often.

What skill did Sofia develop?

options.A: Explaining an idea even when she does not know the exact word
options.C: Avoiding conversations with unfamiliar people
options.D: Learning every possible word before using English

explanation: She learned to paraphrase instead of immediately using translation.

question_text:
A city park replaced some frequently cut grass with wildflower areas. The new areas need less mowing and attract more insects, although signs explain that they may look less tidy at certain times of year.

What is a benefit of the wildflower areas?

options.A: They are cut more frequently than ordinary grass
options.B: They require less maintenance and support insects
options.C: They require more water and fewer insects visit them
options.D: They make every part of the park look tidier all year

explanation: Both reduced mowing and more insects are stated.

question_text:
Before giving a presentation, Oleksii recorded himself practising it on his phone. He noticed that he spoke too quickly in the introduction and rarely looked up from his notes. In the final presentation, he deliberately slowed down and used shorter notes.

How did the recording help Oleksii?

options.A: It allowed him to avoid practising again
options.C: It showed him specific aspects of his delivery to improve
options.D: It showed that his notes were too short to use

explanation: He identified speed and eye-contact issues from the recording.

question_text:
An online shop began showing an estimated repairability score for electronic products. The score considers whether common parts can be replaced and whether repair information is available.

What does the score help customers compare?

options.A: How many apps are installed on the products
options.C: How quickly the products are delivered
options.D: How practical products may be to repair

explanation: The score is based on replaceable parts and repair information.

question_text:
Yana joined a reading challenge that asked participants to read ten books in ten different genres. She normally chose only fantasy, so the challenge introduced her to biographies and science writing, which she had rarely considered before.

What changed because of the challenge?

options.A: Yana tried types of books she did not usually choose
options.C: She read fewer books than before
options.D: She chose only books recommended by friends

explanation: The challenge pushed her beyond her usual fantasy choices.

question_text:
A school replaced long weekly announcements with a short daily message shown on classroom screens. Teachers report that students now remember deadlines better because information is more current and repeated closer to the relevant date.

Why are students remembering deadlines better?

options.A: Every message now contains more information
options.B: They receive shorter, more timely reminders
options.C: Deadlines were removed from the school schedule
options.D: Students receive announcements only once a month

explanation: The messages are current and repeated near the deadline.

question_text:
When Oleh first worked in a café, he tried to memorize every order without writing anything down. After several mistakes, he began using the small order pad provided. His accuracy improved immediately.

What lesson did Oleh learn?

options.A: The café stopped allowing staff to use order pads
options.B: Customers preferred orders that were not written down
options.C: Using a simple tool was more reliable than depending only on memory
options.D: Memorising became easier as the café got busier

explanation: Writing orders down reduced his mistakes.

question_text:
The university library added standing desks near its windows. They are not intended to replace normal desks but to give students another option when they want to change position during long study sessions.

Why were standing desks added?

options.A: To keep students away from the windows
options.B: To force all students to stand while studying
options.C: To reduce the number of study places
options.D: To provide more choice in how students study

explanation: They are an additional option, not a replacement.

question_text:
A volunteer group originally planned monthly clean-up events. However, many people said they could not commit to a whole morning. The group now runs shorter one-hour sessions twice a month, and attendance has increased.

Why did attendance increase?

options.A: The new sessions require a smaller time commitment
options.B: The events became longer and less frequent
options.C: The group stopped advertising the events
options.D: Participants were required to attend every session

explanation: Shorter sessions made participation easier.

question_text:
Eva noticed that she often forgot online passwords and repeatedly reset them. She started using a password manager, which creates and stores strong passwords. She now needs to remember only one main password.

What problem did the password manager solve for Eva?

options.A: It created several new passwords he must memorise
options.B: It reduced the number of passwords she had to remember herself
options.C: It removed the need for any main password
options.D: It made all of his accounts use the same weak password

explanation: The manager stores the other passwords for her.

question_text:
A café tested reusable takeaway cups with a small deposit. Customers receive the deposit back when they return the cup to any participating café. The system is designed to make reuse convenient even for people who do not visit the same café again.

Why can customers return cups to different cafés?

options.A: To ensure only one café can use the system
options.B: To make customers keep every cup permanently
options.C: To make the reuse system easier to use
options.D: To prevent deposits from being returned

explanation: Multiple return points increase convenience.

question_text:
Mykhailo began studying in the same place and at the same time each evening. After several weeks, he found it easier to start working without spending time deciding when and where to study.

What advantage did the routine give Mykhailo?

options.A: He stopped planning any study time in advance
options.B: He had to choose a new study place every day
options.C: He began studying for much shorter periods
options.D: It reduced the effort needed to begin studying

explanation: A fixed routine removed repeated decisions about time and place.

question_text:
A language teacher sometimes asks students to explain a grammar rule to a partner instead of only completing exercises. She says explaining forces students to organise what they know and reveals gaps in understanding.

Why does the teacher use peer explanation?

options.A: It helps students notice whether they truly understand the rule
options.B: It lets students avoid learning the grammar rule
options.C: It replaces all written practice with conversation
options.D: It ensures partners always give the correct explanation

explanation: Explaining makes knowledge gaps visible.

question_text:
After the local cinema introduced cheaper tickets on Tuesday afternoons, attendance at those screenings rose sharply. Evening attendance stayed almost unchanged, suggesting the offer attracted people who were flexible about time.

What can be inferred from the result?

options.A: Evening tickets became much more expensive
options.B: The discount mainly changed when some people chose to visit
options.C: The cinema lost nearly all evening customers
options.D: People stopped going to Tuesday screenings

explanation: Afternoon attendance rose while evenings stayed similar.

question_text:

Why were the videos effective?

options.A: They replaced the need to attend club meetings
options.B: They guaranteed that every student would enjoy the club
options.C: They made the club's activities easier to understand before joining
options.D: They showed only the dates of future events

explanation: The videos showed what meetings were actually like.

options.D: In the library while studying

explanation: The text says he uses them more often in the library.

options.D: Giving students all sections at the same time without breaks

options.B: The route became accessible to more people

explanation: The extension brought the route within walking distance of more residents.

She suggested _____ the meeting until Monday.

options.A: postponed
options.C: postpone
options.D: postponing

explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund in this structure.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I _____ this laptop for three years and it still works well.

options.A: have had
options.C: am having
options.D: have

explanation: Present Perfect is used for a state continuing until now.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

You _____ bring your own calculator; one will be provided.

options.A: must not
options.C: cannot
options.D: should not to

explanation: 'Do not have to' expresses lack of necessity.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The teacher asked me where I _____ the information.

options.A: have found
options.C: had found
options.D: will find

explanation: Reported speech shifts the earlier action to Past Perfect.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I am not used to _____ so early in the morning.

options.A: got up
options.C: to get up
options.D: getting up

explanation: 'Be used to' is followed by a noun or gerund.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

When I called, Marta _____ for her exam, so I did not keep her long.

options.A: was studying
options.C: has studied
options.D: had study

explanation: Past Continuous describes an action in progress at a past moment.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

If he _____ the instructions more carefully, he would not have made that mistake.

options.A: read
options.C: would read
options.D: has read

explanation: Third Conditional uses Past Perfect in the if-clause.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The new sports centre _____ next month.

options.A: is opening by them
options.C: will be opened
options.D: opens been

explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

You _____ have seen Anna at school yesterday; she was at home all day.

options.A: need
options.C: should
options.D: cannot

explanation: 'Cannot have + past participle' expresses impossibility about the past.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I stopped _____ my messages while studying because it distracted me.

options.A: checking
options.C: check
options.D: checked

explanation: 'Stop doing' means cease an activity.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

We _____ dinner when the lights suddenly went out.

options.A: had
options.C: have had
options.D: are having

explanation: Past Continuous sets the background for a shorter past event.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

If I were you, I _____ that email once more before sending it.

options.A: read
options.C: would read
options.D: had read

explanation: Second Conditional advice uses 'would + infinitive'.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The results _____ on the website as soon as they are available.

options.A: published
options.C: are publishing
options.D: will be published

explanation: The subject receives the action, so future passive is required.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

He admitted _____ the wrong file by mistake.

options.A: sending
options.C: send
options.D: sent

explanation: 'Admit' is normally followed by a gerund.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I _____ my keys, so I cannot open the door.

options.A: lost yesterday
options.C: had lost
options.D: am losing

explanation: Present Perfect links a recent past event with a present result.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Unless you _____ now, you will miss the beginning of the lesson.

options.A: left
options.C: leave
options.D: would leave

explanation: After 'unless' in a future condition, use Present Simple.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Students _____ use their phones during the test.

options.A: might
options.C: could
options.D: must not

explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

She told me that she _____ the report the following day.

options.A: would finish
options.C: finishes
options.D: has finished

explanation: In reported speech, 'will' usually shifts to 'would'.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

We decided _____ a short break before continuing.

options.A: taking
options.C: take
options.D: took

explanation: 'Decide' is followed by the infinitive with 'to'.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

This time next week, we _____ our final exams.

options.A: have taken
options.C: will be taking
options.D: were taking

explanation: Future Continuous describes an action in progress at a future time.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

If the weather _____ better yesterday, we would have gone hiking.

options.A: has been
options.C: would be
options.D: had been

explanation: Third Conditional requires Past Perfect in the condition.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The classroom _____ before the students arrived.

options.A: had been cleaned
options.C: was cleaning
options.D: has been clean

explanation: Past Perfect passive shows the cleaning happened before another past action.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

You _____ check the deadline again; I am not completely sure of the date.

options.A: must not
options.C: cannot
options.D: would have

explanation: 'Should' is suitable for advice.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I remember _____ that museum when I was younger.

options.A: visit
options.C: visiting
options.D: visited to

explanation: 'Remember doing' refers to a memory of a past action.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

She _____ English since she was eight years old.

options.A: had studied now
options.C: is studying since
options.D: has studied

explanation: Present Perfect with 'since' describes an activity continuing to the present.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Had I known about the change, I _____ earlier.

options.A: would have arrived
options.C: would arrive
options.D: had arrived

explanation: This is an inverted Third Conditional.

question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The manager said that all applications _____ by Friday.

options.A: have submit
options.C: must submitting
options.D: were submit

explanation: The passive infinitive 'be submitted' is required after 'had to'.
